about: Recalling how God enlightened the English peoples through Augustine’s preaching and miracles, the prayer asks that the hearts of those who stray may return to the unity of God’s truth and that the community may be united in His will.

s01.translation: God, You graciously enlightened the English peoples with the light of true faith through the preaching and miracles of blessed Augustine, Your confessor and bishop. Grant that, through his intercession, the hearts of those who stray may return to the unity of Your truth, and that we may be united in Your will. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, who lives and reigns with You in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, forever and ever.

alignments.gloss: with the light of true faith
the hearts of those who stray
may return to the unity of Your truth
may be united in Your will

w003.explanation: The peoples are described by the plural name Angli. The prayer concerns the English peoples, without defining a modern political state.

w009.explanation: The May 28 feast is that of Augustine of Canterbury, not Monica’s son Augustine of Hippo. Both preaching and miracles belong to Augustine of Canterbury, and both are means of God’s enlightening action.

w013.explanation: Pontifex describes Augustine’s episcopal office. The title does not make Augustine of Canterbury a pope.

w018.explanation: Dignatus es is a perfect deponent expression with God as the active subject. Together with illustrare, it recalls His gracious act of enlightenment, not another agent judging God worthy.

w022.explanation: Ipso refers to Augustine. His intercession accompanies the request, without making him the subject of the return or of the community’s concord.

w025.explanation: The hearts belong to people who stray and are the subject of the requested return. The later nos introduces the distinct request that we may be united in God’s will.
